Use case: identity-preserve. Edit the attached APPROVED Batwalk character portrait into a game sprite animation sheet. The image is the exact model to animate, not a loose inspiration. Preserve its individual character identity, precise face, body proportions, palette, silhouette details and existing accessories. Same Gentle pixel rendering, stepped dark outlines and soft shaded pixel clusters. NO redesign, generic bat replacement, global squash/stretch, text, labels, borders, gradient backdrop, lighting change or 3D style.
Invariants for 尘尘蝠: Scruffy asymmetrical spiky gray fluffball, irregular fur tufts, enormous curled forelock leaning upward, dot eyes, single tiny white fang, cream cheek tufts, tiny dark purple bat wings and feet. Keep distinct tangled jagged outline; do not turn into round smooth generic bat.
Output one transparent PNG sprite sheet: EXACTLY 4 equal columns and 3 equal rows; total 12 poses. Landscape 4:3 layout with square cells. Aim 2048 by 1536 pixels. EVERY cell contains the SAME CHARACTER at the SAME SCALE and camera distance. Leave at least 12% transparent margin on all four sides of EACH cell, including props/wings. No marks on grid boundaries. Space rows and columns evenly; never allow an ear/prop to enter another cell. Actual alpha transparency. Feet/body keep a consistent local position except explicitly moving actions. All props stay small so the bat remains clearly recognizable at Watch size.
Each row is a DIFFERENT action below; read each row LEFT TO RIGHT across four successive keyframes: setup, anticipation, main action, settle. Tell the full specified beat, not four duplicate rest poses. Reuse the original neutral character pose closely for setup where appropriate. Change only the body parts relevant to that action. Return towards the original pose at the end when plausible. Use no entire scene backgrounds, only essential tiny action props.
ROW 1 flap-practice: frame1 the bat hangs UPSIDE DOWN from its TWO ORIGINAL FEET grasping a tiny branch ABOVE it, forelock pointing DOWN, face inverted; frame2 its original little wings open while it remains upside down; frame3 vigorous wings while feet stay attached above; frame4 still inverted proudly panting with wings tucked.
ROW 2 drop-start: frame1 hanging upside down with FEET ABOVE FACE; frame2 lets go and falls upside down below the same branch; frame3 rolls upright in midair and opens its two wings, feet now dangling below; frame4 flutters upward toward the tiny branch.
ROW 3 almost-landing: frame1 flying upright underneath a little perch ABOVE the bat; frame2 flips in midair trying to grasp overhead perch with feet; frame3 somersault misses with embarrassed face; frame4 successfully hangs UPSIDE DOWN with its TWO FEET grasping the ABOVE branch, tuft pointing DOWN.
CRITICAL anatomy: only TWO little original wings and TWO original feet, no hands, arms, added limbs. Hanging means UPSIDE DOWN: feet at top, inverted face near bottom, forelock tip at bottom. No branch underneath an upside-down bat. Preserve the reference curly gray face/fur unchanged. Four columns three rows, generous empty transparent gaps, all poses fit fully into their cell. No text.
